There are checking tools in the tools folder, we these used checking the code?

Is this dissector fuzz-tested with actual capture files?

I have just done some fuzz testing using randpkt and then rewriting the UDP destination port to 7943, then opened the pcap with wireshark and there was no crash or anything. Of course there were tons of malformed packets as expected due to the random packets.

Is there anything else I should do? I assume that everything else is run in the pipeline.

Btw we (Commsignia) have been using this dissector for years internally and there were no issues so far.

A much more productive way to fuzz test is to pass `ENABLE_ASAN=ON` to CMake and run `tools/fuzz-test.sh` on one or more sample captures. As the name implies, randpkt simply generates random payloads. fuzz-test.sh runs `editcap -E ...`, which introduces small random changes to the payloads in your capture files. It also enables strict memory checking.

It would also help if you could attach a sample capture to this MR so that it can be harvested by our fuzz infrastructure.

(We should probably remove references to randpkt from the developer documentation; I'm not sure how useful it is nowadays.)
Thank you, I used the fuzz-test.sh as you suggested, found no issues. Also added a sample pcap to test/captures/.
No need to attach pcap on test/captures but directly on this MR

[c2p_sample.pcap](/uploads/c5266461958c0727b20f7ed466224c95/c2p_sample.pcap)

Thanks for the clarification, I removed from test/captures and attached here.

You are right, I don't expect any other dissectors using these, so I moved everything to the .c file
This and the next few items all have the same filter name.  Would it be more useful to give them more descriptive filter names?

I prefer having this as-is. Since e.g. this "angle" type is used for several STI types, it wouldn't give us much benefit if the filter is c2p.sti_value_angle, because even then we would need to filter on the sti_type as well.
So a meaningful filter in both cases (with and without descriptive filter name for the value) is: e.g. `c2p.sti_type == 3 && c2p.sti_value == 13` (`c2p.sti_type == 3 && c2p.sti_value_angle == 13`)
I didn't check whether values have the same meaning across different value fields - whatever is most useful for you.
